doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Never invited to Lincoln Center or Monterey
summary: Hamilton criticizes jazz on TV, says Lincoln Center and the Monterey festival have never invited him, and guesses he told the wrong person off.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Which is cool. I guess we covered all bases in regards to -- I don’t know -­ unfortunately I really don’t know too much about what the scene is today, the so called jazz scene. I listen to that program on BET here which is a jazz station on T.V. but they have a lot of people on there that got nothing to do with jazz. They call it jazz.
Well you are here in New York so you have seen the entire development of Lincoln Center. What do you think of that whole development?
Well I am glad you asked me that.
I am glad I asked you that too while the tape is still running.

For someone unknown reason why, they have never invited me to play there. Those people have never invited me to even attend. Those people -- plus the fact I think that so called Marsalis Jazz Orchestra -- they need to bring something new in there, something different. If they were to give me a shot, I would be different in there. I have never been invited. So -- as a matter of fact I have never been there. I have no idea what it’s like.
I am shocked to be told that. I am absolutely shocked
What is that festival that they have up in San Francisco?
San Francisco Jazz Festival?
Is that the festival?
Monterey is down there.
I have never been invited to Monterey ever.
That is impossible.
I have never been invited.
I mean Monterey they are celebrating their 50th year.
I have never been invited man.
I find that flabbergasting.
That is the truth. I have never been invited.
Do you have any suspicion as to why -- I mean Monterey or -­
Somebody doesn’t dig me. Somewhere along the line -­
You must have ruffled someone’s feathers.
I probably told the wrong person to kiss my butt, you know. You got to watch that.
When you are striving to be your own man sometimes you have to, you know -- but I am surprised at that. Here is Stanley Crouch writing the notes -­
They never invited me over there man.
And he is from California.
Never over there. Never invited me.
That is unbelievable. Maybe we sent them a copy of this.

I have learned -- I am cool about it. It bothered me at one time but it doesn’t bother me now because they lose. But you know the stuff that they play, that I hear, that they play, it’s -- I ain’t going to say nothing about it because -­
